On the other side, the exact supplied illustrated Skyy has reached for its handle to let him through. Capture the instant he notices her matching bomber. Keep both jacket fronts legible, her hand clear of the chest, and their attention on one another. A single practical window light defines the black satin and sherpa. No posing toward camera.

SkyyRose. Use source-bound casting and wardrobe. The illustrated Skyy design stays unchanged across scenes. Real people remain photographic. No added captions, slogans or invented signage; preserve authentic garment lettering. No floating roses, thrones, presenter gestures or synchronized smiles.

Black Rose br-006 is the exact sherpa bomber worn by the original video performer. Preserve source construction, closures, material, hood, panel shapes and marks. Canonical garment references control wardrobe. Mascot archive controls outfit reference only; supplied image.png controls her face, hair and proportions.

      "prompt": "[SCENE]
Interior commuter train vestibule, mid-journey. The narrow corridor between two carriages — scuffed linoleum underfoot, brushed-steel door frame, a single rectangular window set into the connecting door casting the only meaningful light. Late afternoon, overcast exterior softening the source to a cool 6200K ambient skylight that rakes across the vestibule at 45° camera-right. The moment is suspended: he has just registered her through the door glass.

[PRODUCT PLACEMENT]
Two Black Rose br-006 sherpa bomber jackets — one worn by the real male performer, one worn by the illustrated Skyy figure. Both jacket fronts face the viewer at oblique three-quarter angles through the door plane. Sherpa collar, ribbed cuffs, snap-closure chest panels, embroidered lettering and hood construction preserved identically on both garments. Black satin shell catches the window light as a narrow specular ribbon along each shoulder seam. Sherpa panels absorb the same light as dense matte texture. No garment detail obscured by overlap or shadow fill. Authentic embroidered lettering on both jacket fronts remains legible — no distortion, no invented text.

[HUMAN ELEMENT]
The real male performer stands on the near side of the interior train door, weight shifted slightly forward, one hand resting against the door frame — fingers relaxed, knuckles visible, natural skin texture. His gaze has just landed on her through the glass: head turned 15° toward the door, chin slightly lowered, expression caught mid-recognition. The illustrated Skyy — face, hair, and proportions drawn directly from supplied image.png, rendered in her established illustration style without photographic conversion — stands on the far side of the door, her hand extended and already closing around the door handle, wrist angled naturally, fingers wrapped, palm clear of her jacket chest. Her illustrated eyes are directed through the glass toward him, not toward camera. Neither figure poses toward camera. No synchronized smiles. No presenter gestures.

[ENVIRONMENT DETAILS]
Scuffed grey linoleum floor reflecting a faint smear of window light. Brushed-steel door surround with visible wear at the push-plate. A rubber door gasket frames the glass panel. Faint motion blur in the background carriage beyond her shoulder suggests the train is moving. A fold-down luggage hook on the near wall. The glass between them carries a faint reflection ghost — his jacket silhouette visible as a secondary layer on the door surface.

[LIGHTING]
Primary source: single practical rectangular window set into the connecting door, 6200K overcast exterior skylight, large diffused quality, entering at 45° camera-right. Light defines the black satin shell with a controlled specular ribbon and wraps the sherpa collar in soft graduated illumination. Shadow behavior: soft falloff with gradient transition on the near side of each figure, deep shadow side with selective fill on their respective camera-left edges. No fill added from camera direction — shadows are earned. The glass panel introduces a secondary bounce: a faint cool reflection off the steel frame lifts detail in the illustrated Skyy's hand and jacket front without flattening the shadow structure. No practical interior cabin lighting bleeds into the vestibule.

[LENS & CAMERA]
Shot on 50mm standard, aperture f/2.8, shallow depth of field with focus split between the door handle at her hand and his face in the near plane — both sharp enough to read expression and garment detail, background carriage falling to soft bokeh. Camera positioned at standing eye-level, slight 5° cant toward the door to compress the vestibule depth. No camera-facing angles for either subject.

[ATMOSPHERE]
Intimate and suspended — the held breath before a door opens. Cool, slightly industrial air quality. The illustrated and photographic worlds coexist without commentary, as though this is simply how this train is populated. Quiet tension of mutual recognition. No warmth added artificially — the scene earns its intimacy from proximity and light, not color grading.

[COLOR PALETTE]
Dominant: matte black and off-white sherpa across both jacket fronts. Secondary: cool brushed steel grey of the door frame and linoleum. Accent: the narrow warm-neutral skin tone of his hand against the steel frame. Contrast level: high between satin and shadow, low and unified across the mid-tones of the vestibule environment.

[STYLE REFERENCE]
In the style of Erwin Olaf, Nadav Kander, and Jamie Hawkesworth. Editorial commercial photography — narrative storyboard register, not advertising tableau. Stillness with implied motion. Illustration and photography coexist within a single coherent frame without style collision.

[QUALITY MARKERS]
Cinematic depth. Hyper-realistic fabric texture on satin shell and sherpa pile. Natural hand and skin detail on the male performer. Illustrated Skyy rendered at source-faithful fidelity — face, hair, proportions, and illustration style drawn from supplied image.png without photographic conversion or stylistic drift. Door glass reads as glass: reflective, slightly refractive, separating two presences without erasing either.

[AVOID]
no AI artifacts, no warped or smeared text, no fake words baked into the image,
no plastic look, no waxy surface, no cartoonish rendering,
no extra fingers, no extra limbs, no melted geometry, no doubled subjects,
no oversaturated HDR, no HDR halos, no oversharpened look,
no flat fluorescent lighting, no harsh on-camera flash,
no generic stock photography poses, no cliché compositions,
no random unrelated brand logos, no watermarks, no signatures,
no AI sheen on hair or skin, no doll-like rendering, no airbrush look,
no flat solid color bands, no empty rectangular areas, no dull gradient zones,
no AI uncanny faces, no warped facial geometry, no asymmetric eyes,
no extra teeth, no melted facial features, no warped fingers or hands,
no plastic skin, no orange-tan skin, no over-smoothed retouching,
no doll eyes, no misaligned facial features, no rubber-like skin texture,
no warped product label text, no garbled letters, no fake brand names,
no melted typography, no doubled labels, no fictional logos,
no stale stock photography aesthetic, no synthetic stock-photo look,
no over-staged feeling, no unrealistically clean environments,
no floating roses, no thrones, no presenter gestures, no synchronized smiles,
no posing toward camera, no added captions, no invented signage, no slogans,
no style bleed between illustration register and photographic register — maintain coexistence without merger,
no alteration to illustrated Skyy's face, hair, or proportions beyond what is supplied,
no substitution of a photographic human for the illustrated Skyy figure.
